title: Getting people to care is the hardest part: lead with the user's transformation, not your product
summary: Alex argues the hardest part of launching anything (apps, music, art) is getting people to care, not making it. He says image and inspiration drive attention, and marketing should centre the user's better future rather than "download my app." Persistence through early indifference is key.

principles.text: Getting people to care is harder than building the product; most launches fail on attention, not quality.
principles.quote: Getting people to care is the hardest part. Everyone has so much going on with their life. Why would they care about you and what you've released?

principles.text: Early silence is what kills most ambitions, so expect it and don't read it as proof you aren't good enough.
principles.quote: they start to think like I'm not good enough or this is so hard or like am I delusional, am I crazy, this that the other and they maybe give up.

principles.text: For creator-led products, your personal image and lifestyle drive whether people care about your work.
principles.quote: If I'm just a young guy in London making exceptional music, I dress well, I smell good, I drive a nice car, my captions on Instagram are on point

principles.text: Match your public persona to the audience you want to reach, even if it means not tying your name to what you love.
principles.quote: I can't tie my name too much to software. Even though I love it, I can't tie my name too much to software.

principles.text: Put the user first in all marketing: show their life could be better, instead of asking them to download your app.
principles.quote: Instead of being like download my app, you're like transform your life. These are very different things.

principles.text: Inspire people to sell to them, and stay persistent and consistent through being ignored on day one.
principles.quote: If you can inspire someone, you can sell to them.
